newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Femsa says it becoming leaner, meaner.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Femsa says it becoming leaner, meaner.

text.p: Mexican beverage company Fomentos Economicos Mexicanos S.A. says it will emerge from Mexico's economic crisis a better company -- more focused and less saddled with debt.
Mexico's economy has been slow in getting up from the knockout punch delivered by the peso crash, but company officials say they aren't wasting any time in getting ready to cash in on a recovery.
"Each time we have a crisis here, we learn. We are practically PHDs at crises," joked Jose Antonio Fernandez, CEO of Femsa, in an interview with Reuters.

"This may sound crazy, but these last two years have given us the chance to look inwardly at the company instead of out -- to plan, think, adjust costs ... with only the slightest pick-up in the economy, you will see a big difference in our sales. We will be a much better company than two years ago."

Fernandez sees a slow Mexican economy in the months ahead. The company's best indicator of demand, how much individual consumers spend at their Oxxo convenience stores, is still falling in real terms from 1995 levels.
"I think we might have to wait until next year to see the recovery ... probably the second quarter of 1997," he said.
Femsa has refocused its beer business in the past two years -- and stemmed a decade-long slide in market share -- and now wants to shore up its Coca-Cola business by restructuring debt.
